arguments.name: destination
arguments.type: square floating-point matrix for inverse result

semantics.summary: Calculates the inverse of the square source matrix and writes the result to the destination matrix of the same type and dimensions.
side-effects: Writes the inverse matrix to the destination operand.

printed-pages: Supplied 469-page manual, Chapter 13, printed p. 13-30 detailed description and worked example; combined update scan, Chapter 13, printed p. 13-39; German companion book, printed p. 475
notes: The detailed 3.5 addendum definition and worked example specify destination-first MAT INV b()=a(): the inverse of source a() is written to destination b().
The German companion book independently confirms destination-first MAT INV i()=m() (printed p. 475).

The supplied manual command summary on printed p. 13-16 (combined update scan, p. 13-22) reverses the operands as MAT INV a()=b(); the detailed definition/example and companion-book confirmation support treating that summary notation as a source typo. The summary discrepancy is retained here for traceability, not as a second accepted syntax.
The destination-first syntax is source-documented; runtime behavior and numerical edge cases remain unimplemented and untested.

support.pending-reason: No matrix-inverse implementation or executable reference-interpreter conformance tests are registered.
